steps.title: Shuck an oyster
steps.prompt: Put the stages of shucking an oyster for the half shell in order, from the cooler to the ice. One stage does not belong.
steps: Scrub the shells under cold running water, and throw out any that gape and will not close when tapped
Guard your holding hand with a folded towel or a cut-resistant glove, and hold the oyster cup side down, hinge towards you
Work the tip of the oyster knife into the hinge and twist until the shell pops
Wipe the blade clean of mud and grit before it goes back in
Slide the blade along the inside of the top shell to cut the muscle, and lift the top shell away
Keeping the cup level, run the blade under the oyster to free it from the bottom shell
With the oyster freed in its cup, check it by eye for grit and chipped shell, and smell it: an oyster that smells off is thrown away
Set it on crushed ice in its liquor, the salty juice in the shell, and send it at once
steps.distractor: Pour off the liquor and rinse the oyster under the tap so it looks clean
steps.why: Clean, live shells come first, and the hand is guarded before any knife goes in. The hinge is popped and the blade wiped so no grit falls in; the top muscle is cut, then the bottom, with the cup level. The liquor is part of the taste and is never poured away or rinsed off.

match.title: The Louisiana larder at work
match.prompt: Match each ingredient of the Louisiana larder to where it does its work, in the kitchen or on the Brennan's menu.
pairs: Stirred into gumbo off the heat, or pinched over the bowl at the table
Sliced into half-moons and browned first, so its smoky fat seasons the pot
Seasons the Creole sauce on the New Orleans Shrimp & Grits
The grainy, sharp backbone of a pink Creole rémoulade
Blended with dark roast coffee and poured with hot milk as café au lait
Cooked in its own pot, the rice under the Seafood Gumbo
Thin toasted crisps on the Creole Caesar, in place of croutons
Glazes the peaches beside the Roasted Rohan Duck Breast on the dinner tasting

match.title: Crabmeat grades
match.prompt: Match each grade of picked Louisiana blue crabmeat to what it is.
pairs: The two large muscles that drive the swimming legs, whole and white
Large body pieces and broken jumbo, the grade just below jumbo lump
Smaller flakes of lump mixed with some white body meat
Fine white flake from the body, for crab cakes, dips and stuffings
Darker, pinkish brown meat, firmer and sweeter with a stronger flavour, and the least costly
